positions.name: OwnedIntelligenceAsKeptAsset
positions.frame: what distinguishes intelligence you keep from intelligence you merely rent, and what follows for how substrate and perspective are valued?
positions.why: Both expressions share the same antithetical, aphoristic-technical register (owned vs. rented; commodity vs. asset) and the same underlying value appeal to autonomy and self-enhancement — possession as the good, borrowing as its lesser counterpart. The relational and power reads converge too: perspective is cast as retained capital against a disposable substrate, and that valuation itself does the persuasive work. Conviction readings differ slightly in register (src-2 lands as a flat claim, src-3 as a more creed-like principle), but both point the same direction — toward a single distinction between owned and rented intelligence — so they cohere as one group despite that gradient rather than splitting into separate positions.
